openQuestions.question: Where should Ungroup place included parts whose simultaneous timing cannot be represented on the destination track without overlap?
openQuestions.why: Saved clips can contain a four-track composition, while timeline clips on one track cannot overlap. The current source defines which trimmed parts survive but does not define a track-placement policy for overlapping parts. Keep the copied group and draft intact; do not infer flattening, shifts or alternate track mapping. This also covers embedded composition framing, stacking or audio settings that cannot be preserved by the destination track without an additional mapping.

openQuestions.question: How should Ungroup transfer a group's nondefault source rectangle, volume or mute to its included parts?
openQuestions.why: Group-level crop and audio adjustments can change the picture or sound even when parts are sequential. Their disposition on Ungroup is not specified. Until a transfer policy is selected, a group with a non-full-frame source rectangle, volume other than 100%, or mute enabled cannot be ungrouped; explain the applicable adjustment and retain the complete copied group, draft and selection. The supported neutral-group path retains each part's own framing and audio settings without resetting them.

traceGaps.explanation: Representative Open invocation only. Shared behavior preserves draft-first/project-second semantics, but the single-parent frame representation cannot encode multiple triggers and captured conditional return targets. Do not treat the representative frame as exhaustive.
Return to captured stopped editor or retained failed-operation context; dynamic return cannot be fully expressed by one target.
Complete description expansion cannot silently replace conflicting destination-track framing/audio. Identify conflict and insert nothing until a preservation policy is selected.

The saved source-rectangle frame represents invocation from occurrence properties. Native edit-video add-crop, add-crop-full-frame and add-crop-canceled alternates explicitly capture the staged-Add invocation and return. A separately illustrated staged-Add rectangle invocation remains uncovered; do not treat the representative frame parent as a runtime override of those flows.

Ungroup also requires included parts whose timing and existing composition framing, stacking and audio can be represented on the destination track without overlap or a new mapping. Placement for overlapping/multitrack parts, or other composition settings that cannot be preserved there, remains undesigned. Preserve the original group and draft; no automatic track mapping, flattening, property reset or timing change is selected.

The group source rectangle, volume and mute have no selected transfer policy. Ungroup is unavailable when the group's source rectangle is not full frame, its volume is not 100%, or mute is on, even for sequential parts. Keep all copied group data, draft and selection unchanged. Enabled Ungroup requires neutral group adjustments and a representation preserving each included part's own source rectangle, volume, mute and the current composition result; do not reset settings, bake adjustments or infer transfer algorithms.
